model.context: Flying fish, flying halfbeaks, halfbeaks and needlefish from the repo's observed allometry (Daane 2021 Data S1A copy).
model.name: Two-phase distal growth-zone programme: tip-saturated limit of a morphogen-gradient fin-growth model

numerical_results: Flying fish minus halfbeak fin/SL at SL 20 cm: 0.566, of which 0.576 from c and -0.010 from a
Species level (flying fish - flying halfbeak): delta c 0.384, two-stage bootstrap 95% CI 0.248-0.488
Species level (flying fish - halfbeak): delta c 0.591, two-stage bootstrap 95% CI 0.531-0.639
Species level (flying fish - needlefish): delta c 0.653, two-stage bootstrap 95% CI 0.594-0.695

Per-species c: Hirundichthys rondeleti 0.711, Exocoetus volitans 0.765, Cheilopogon furcatus 0.730, Euleptorhamphus velox 0.274, Hemiramphus brasiliensis 0.155, Oxyporhamphus micropterus 0.397, Hyporhamphus unifasciatus 0.121, Belone belone 0.078, Strongylura marina 0.080
open_questions: Is the high flying-fish c a higher outgrowth rate, a longer-lived growth zone, or a larger saturated zone? Longitudinal imaging of the distal fin margin and a graded perturbation series would separate them.
Data-compatible gradient lengths predict production elasticities of fin/SL from 0.08 to 0.99: a dose series discriminates them.
Phase 1 (below 1.68 cm SL) is unobserved; larval specimens are needed to test whether an early burst exists.
The flying-halfbeak group mixes two species with different proportions; per-species fits need more specimens.
parameter_unknowns: r, s, D, k, P, K are not separately identified; only the composite c and the extrapolated intercept a are fitted.
A power law L = b SL^alpha fits modestly better (AIC) in every group; the linear programme is an interpretable, untested reading, not the preferred statistical form.
The morphogen is hypothetical; no molecule is assigned to m(x).
